sanskrit.deva:
सनत्सुजात यदिमां परार्थां ब्राह्मीं वाचं वदसि हि विश्वरूपाम् ।
परां हि कार्येषु सुदुर्लभां कथां प्रब्रूहि मे वाक्यमेवं कुमार ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sanatsujāta yad imāṃ parārthāṃ brāhmīṃ vācaṃ vadasi hi viśvarūpām |
parāṃ hi kāryeṣu sudurlabhāṃ kathāṃ prabrūhi me vākyam evaṃ kumāra || 1 ||

lines.iast: sanatsujāta yad imāṃ parārthāṃ brāhmīṃ vācaṃ vadasi hi viśvarūpām
lines.deva: सनत्सुजात यदिमां परार्थां ब्राह्मीं वाचं वदसि हि विश्वरूपाम्

lines.iast: parāṃ hi kāryeṣu sudurlabhāṃ kathāṃ prabrūhi me vākyam evaṃ kumāra
lines.deva: परां हि कार्येषु सुदुर्लभां कथां प्रब्रूहि मे वाक्यमेवं कुमार

padaccheda.iast: sanatsujāta yat imām para-arthām brāhmīm vācam vadasi hi viśva-rūpām parām hi kāryeṣu su-durlabhām kathām prabrūhi me vākyam evam kumāra
padaccheda.deva: सनत्सुजात यत् इमाम् पर-अर्थाम् ब्राह्मीम् वाचम् वदसि हि विश्व-रूपाम् पराम् हि कार्येषु सु-दुर्लभाम् कथाम् प्रब्रूहि मे वाक्यम् एवम् कुमार

translations.text: Sanatsujāta, since you speak this speech concerning Brahman, of the highest meaning and of many forms, a supreme discourse, very hard to come by (even to hear) in the manifold world, tell me words of this kind, O youth (for you alone are fit to tell them).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the adhyāya: now, after the means, brahmacarya and the rest, the third and fourth adhyāyas begin, to set forth Brahman, which is reached by those means. Having heard of the means, brahmacarya and the rest, and longing to know Brahman, Dhṛtarāṣṭra speaks.

Śaṅkara: yat = yasmāt, since; parārthām = of excellent meaning; brāhmīm = connected with Brahman; viśvarūpām = of many forms; kāryeṣu = among the classes of effects, the manifold world; sudurlabhām = not possible even to hear. Since you speak such speech about Brahman, the means to the highest human end, you alone are fit to speak it.

sanskrit.deva:
नैतद्ब्रह्म त्वरमाणेन लभ्यं यन्मां पृच्छस्यभिषङ्गेण राजन् ।
बुद्धौ प्रलीने मनसि प्रचिन्त्या विद्या हि सा ब्रह्मचर्येण लभ्या ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
naitad brahma tvaramāṇena labhyaṃ yan māṃ pṛcchasy abhiṣaṅgeṇa rājan |
buddhau pralīne manasi pracintyā vidyā hi sā brahmacaryeṇa labhyā || 2 ||

lines.iast: naitad brahma tvaramāṇena labhyaṃ yan māṃ pṛcchasy abhiṣaṅgeṇa rājan
lines.deva: नैतद्ब्रह्म त्वरमाणेन लभ्यं यन्मां पृच्छस्यभिषङ्गेण राजन्

lines.iast: buddhau pralīne manasi pracintyā vidyā hi sā brahmacaryeṇa labhyā
lines.deva: बुद्धौ प्रलीने मनसि प्रचिन्त्या विद्या हि सा ब्रह्मचर्येण लभ्या

padaccheda.iast: na etat brahma tvaramāṇena labhyam yat mām pṛcchasi abhiṣaṅgeṇa rājan buddhau pralīne manasi pracintyā vidyā hi sā brahmacaryeṇa labhyā
padaccheda.deva: न एतत् ब्रह्म त्वरमाणेन लभ्यम् यत् माम् पृच्छसि अभिषङ्गेण राजन् बुद्धौ प्रलीने मनसि प्रचिन्त्या विद्या हि सा ब्रह्मचर्येण लभ्या

grammar.en: past passive participle n. loc. sg.

translations.text: This Brahman, about which you ask me so eagerly, O king, is not gained by one who is in haste. When the mind is dissolved in the understanding, that knowledge is to be contemplated; it is gained by brahmacarya (as it will be described).

notes: Śaṅkara: buddhau = in the understanding, whose nature is resolve (adhyavasāya); pralīne manasi = when the mind, whose nature is intention and doubt (saṃkalpa-vikalpa), turns back from objects and becomes still in its own self. The knowledge to be contemplated then is gained by the brahmacarya about to be described.

sanskrit.deva:
आद्यां विद्यां वदसि हि सत्यरूपां या प्राप्यते ब्रह्मचर्येण सद्भिः ।
यां प्राप्यैनं मर्त्यभावं त्यजन्ति या वै विद्या गुरुवृद्धेषु नित्या ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ādyāṃ vidyāṃ vadasi hi satyarūpāṃ yā prāpyate brahmacaryeṇa sadbhiḥ |
yāṃ prāpyainaṃ martyabhāvaṃ tyajanti yā vai vidyā guruvṛddheṣu nityā || 3 ||

lines.iast: ādyāṃ vidyāṃ vadasi hi satyarūpāṃ yā prāpyate brahmacaryeṇa sadbhiḥ
lines.deva: आद्यां विद्यां वदसि हि सत्यरूपां या प्राप्यते ब्रह्मचर्येण सद्भिः

lines.iast: yāṃ prāpyainaṃ martyabhāvaṃ tyajanti yā vai vidyā guruvṛddheṣu nityā
lines.deva: यां प्राप्यैनं मर्त्यभावं त्यजन्ति या वै विद्या गुरुवृद्धेषु नित्या

padaccheda.iast: ādyām vidyām vadasi hi satya-rūpām yā prāpyate brahmacaryeṇa sadbhiḥ yām prāpya enam martya-bhāvam tyajanti yā vai vidyā guru-vṛddheṣu nityā
padaccheda.deva: आद्याम् विद्याम् वदसि हि सत्य-रूपाम् या प्राप्यते ब्रह्मचर्येण सद्भिः याम् प्राप्य एनम् मर्त्य-भावम् त्यजन्ति या वै विद्या गुरु-वृद्धेषु नित्या

words.meaning: in those grown through the teacher

translations.text: You speak of (and ask me to tell) the first knowledge, whose form is truth, which is attained by the good through brahmacarya, attaining which they abandon this mortal state, the knowledge that is constant in those grown (in it) through the teacher.

notes: Śaṅkara: ādyām = whose object is Brahman, the first of all; satyarūpām = whose form is the highest truth: ‘tell me’ (you say). Or else: ādyām = not an effect, not having the unreal world for its object. Therefore it is gained only by one who is not in haste, who has the means, brahmacarya and the rest, and whose inner organ is withdrawn. guruvṛddheṣu = in disciples grown by the teacher through the giving of knowledge and the rest; nityā = fixed, certain.

sanskrit.deva:
ब्रह्मचर्येण या विद्या शक्या वेदितुमञ्जसा ।
तत्कथं ब्रह्मचर्यं स्यादेतद्विद्वन्ब्रवीहि मे ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
brahmacaryeṇa yā vidyā śakyā veditum añjasā |
tat kathaṃ brahmacaryaṃ syād etad vidvan bravīhi me || 4 ||

lines.iast: brahmacaryeṇa yā vidyā śakyā veditum añjasā
lines.deva: ब्रह्मचर्येण या विद्या शक्या वेदितुमञ्जसा

lines.iast: tat kathaṃ brahmacaryaṃ syād etad vidvan bravīhi me
lines.deva: तत्कथं ब्रह्मचर्यं स्यादेतद्विद्वन्ब्रवीहि मे

padaccheda.iast: brahmacaryeṇa yā vidyā śakyā veditum añjasā tat katham brahmacaryam syāt etat vidvan bravīhi me
padaccheda.deva: ब्रह्मचर्येण या विद्या शक्या वेदितुम् अञ्जसा तत् कथम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् स्यात् एतत् विद्वन् ब्रवीहि मे

translations.text: The knowledge that can be known directly through brahmacarya: how is that brahmacarya (to be practised)? Tell me this, O learned one.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: when this was said, Dhṛtarāṣṭra speaks in order to learn what brahmacarya is. He does not comment on the verse itself.

sanskrit.deva:
आचार्ययोनिमिह ये प्रविश्य भूत्वा गर्भं ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति ।
इहैव ते शास्त्रकारा भवन्ति विहाय देहं परमं यान्ति सत्यम् ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ācāryayonim iha ye praviśya bhūtvā garbhaṃ brahmacaryaṃ caranti |
ihaiva te śāstrakārā bhavanti vihāya dehaṃ paramaṃ yānti satyam || 5 ||

lines.iast: ācāryayonim iha ye praviśya bhūtvā garbhaṃ brahmacaryaṃ caranti
lines.deva: आचार्ययोनिमिह ये प्रविश्य भूत्वा गर्भं ब्रह्मचर्यं चरन्ति

lines.iast: ihaiva te śāstrakārā bhavanti vihāya dehaṃ paramaṃ yānti satyam
lines.deva: इहैव ते शास्त्रकारा भवन्ति विहाय देहं परमं यान्ति सत्यम्

padaccheda.iast: ācārya-yonim iha ye praviśya bhūtvā garbham brahmacaryam caranti iha eva te śāstra-kārāḥ bhavanti vihāya deham paramam yānti satyam
padaccheda.deva: आचार्य-योनिम् इह ये प्रविश्य भूत्वा गर्भम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् चरन्ति इह एव ते शास्त्र-काराः भवन्ति विहाय देहम् परमम् यान्ति सत्यम्

words.meaning: the womb that is the teacher

translations.text: Those who, entering here the womb that is the teacher and becoming an embryo (his disciples), practise brahmacarya, become even here makers of treatises; leaving the body, they go to the highest, the True.

notes: Śaṅkara: ācāryayonim praviśya = going to the teacher; bhūtvā garbham = becoming disciples by approaching him and the rest; brahmacaryam = service of the teacher and the rest; śāstrakārāḥ = learned men, authors of treatises. Then, weary of childhood and the rest, they become brāhmaṇas, and when the karma that has begun to bear fruit is spent they leave the body and attain the True, the supreme Self, marked by truth and the rest.
The edition prints vadanti; read caranti, as the bhāṣya has it (caranti kurvanti).

sanskrit.deva:
अस्मिꣳल्लोके विजयन्तीह कामान्ब्राह्मीं स्थितिमनुतितिक्षमाणाः ।
त आत्मानं निर्हरन्तीह देहान्मुञ्जादिषीकामिव धीरभावात् ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
asmim̐l loke vijayantīha kāmān brāhmīṃ sthitim anutitikṣamāṇāḥ |
ta ātmānaṃ nirharantīha dehān muñjād iṣīkām iva dhīrabhāvāt || 6 ||

lines.iast: asmim̐l loke vijayantīha kāmān brāhmīṃ sthitim anutitikṣamāṇāḥ
lines.deva: अस्मिꣳल्लोके विजयन्तीह कामान्ब्राह्मीं स्थितिमनुतितिक्षमाणाः

lines.iast: ta ātmānaṃ nirharantīha dehān muñjād iṣīkām iva dhīrabhāvāt
lines.deva: त आत्मानं निर्हरन्तीह देहान्मुञ्जादिषीकामिव धीरभावात्

padaccheda.iast: asmin loke vijayanti iha kāmān brāhmīm sthitim anutitikṣamāṇāḥ te ātmānam nirharanti iha dehāt muñjāt iṣīkām iva dhīra-bhāvāt
padaccheda.deva: अस्मिन् लोके विजयन्ति इह कामान् ब्राह्मीम् स्थितिम् अनुतितिक्षमाणाः ते आत्मानम् निर्हरन्ति इह देहात् मुञ्जात् इषीकाम् इव धीर-भावात्

translations.text: In this world they conquer desires here, holding patiently, day after day, to the standing in Brahman; by steadfastness they draw out the Self here from the body, like the inner stalk from muñja grass.

notes: Śaṅkara: brāhmīṃ sthitim = the standing in Brahman alone; anutitikṣamāṇāḥ = bearing it day after day; ātmānam nirharanti = drawing out from body, senses and the rest their witness, pure consciousness, they set it apart. As one draws out the stalk that lies within the muñja grass, so, drawing it out from the five sheaths, they attain the Self of all; dhīrabhāvāt = by firmness. He cites Kaṭha 2.3.17 (‘the Puruṣa, the size of a thumb … one should draw him out from one’s own body with firmness, as the stalk from the muñja grass’).

sanskrit.deva:
शरीरमेतौ कुरुतः पिता माता च भारत ।
आचार्यतस्तु यज्जन्म तत्सत्यं वै तथामृतम् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śarīram etau kurutaḥ pitā mātā ca bhārata |
ācāryatas tu yaj janma tat satyaṃ vai tathāmṛtam || 7 ||

lines.iast: śarīram etau kurutaḥ pitā mātā ca bhārata
lines.deva: शरीरमेतौ कुरुतः पिता माता च भारत

lines.iast: ācāryatas tu yaj janma tat satyaṃ vai tathāmṛtam
lines.deva: आचार्यतस्तु यज्जन्म तत्सत्यं वै तथामृतम्

padaccheda.iast: śarīram etau kurutaḥ pitā mātā ca bhārata ācāryataḥ tu yat janma tat satyam vai tathā amṛtam
padaccheda.deva: शरीरम् एतौ कुरुतः पिता माता च भारत आचार्यतः तु यत् जन्म तत् सत्यम् वै तथा अमृतम्

translations.text: These two, father and mother, make the body, O Bhārata; but the birth that is from the teacher, that is true, and deathless too.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: in ‘ācāryayonim iha’ (verse 5) the teacher was shown to be a womb. How can the teacher, apart from mother and father, be a womb? To this doubt he says that the teacher alone is truly the begetter.

Śaṅkara: mother and father make the body; they do not beget the self in its own nature. The birth as the two bodies is untrue; the birth from the teacher, as Brahman, being, consciousness and bliss without a second, is true, real, and deathless, free from perishing. So he alone is the begetter. He cites Praśna 6.8 (‘you are our father, who take us across to the far shore of ignorance’) and Āpastamba (‘he begets him through knowledge; that is the best birth; mother and father beget the body only’).

sanskrit.deva:
स आवृणोत्यमृतं संप्रयच्छंस्तस्मै न द्रुह्येत्कृतमस्य जानन् ।
गुरुं शिष्यो नित्यमभिवादयीत स्वाध्यायमिच्छेच्च सदाप्रमत्तः ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa āvṛṇoty amṛtaṃ saṃprayacchaṃs tasmai na druhyet kṛtam asya jānan |
guruṃ śiṣyo nityam abhivādayīta svādhyāyam icchec ca sadāpramattaḥ || 8 ||

lines.iast: sa āvṛṇoty amṛtaṃ saṃprayacchaṃs tasmai na druhyet kṛtam asya jānan
lines.deva: स आवृणोत्यमृतं संप्रयच्छंस्तस्मै न द्रुह्येत्कृतमस्य जानन्

lines.iast: guruṃ śiṣyo nityam abhivādayīta svādhyāyam icchec ca sadāpramattaḥ
lines.deva: गुरुं शिष्यो नित्यमभिवादयीत स्वाध्यायमिच्छेच्च सदाप्रमत्तः

padaccheda.iast: saḥ āvṛṇoti amṛtam saṃprayacchan tasmai na druhyet kṛtam asya jānan gurum śiṣyaḥ nityam abhivādayīta svādhyāyam icchet ca sadā apramattaḥ
padaccheda.deva: सः आवृणोति अमृतम् संप्रयच्छन् तस्मै न द्रुह्येत् कृतम् अस्य जानन् गुरुम् शिष्यः नित्यम् अभिवादयीत स्वाध्यायम् इच्छेत् च सदा अप्रमत्तः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: He (the teacher) fills (the disciple) with the deathless, bestowing it (as his Self); knowing what he has done (for him), one should not wrong him. The disciple should always salute the teacher (and worship him as a god), and should desire study of scripture (hearing and the rest), ever heedful.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: since the attaining of the highest human end depends on the teacher, therefore (the verse follows).

Śaṅkara: āvṛṇoti = fills; amṛtam = Brahman, full bliss, which he bestows as the disciple’s Self; tasmai na druhyet = one should do him no wrong. He cites Śvetāśvatara 6.23 (‘to the great soul who has supreme devotion to God, and to the teacher as to God, these things, when told, shine forth’) and Āpastamba (‘one should never wrong him, for he begets him through knowledge’). kṛtam asya jānan: the genitive asya stands for the instrumental: knowing the help done to oneself by him. abhivādayīta: one should worship the teacher as a god; svādhyāyam icchet = one should be intent on hearing and the rest; apramattaḥ = free from heedlessness.

sanskrit.deva:
शिष्यवृत्तिक्रमेणैव विद्यामाप्नोति यः शुचिः ।
ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतस्यास्य प्रथमः पाद उच्यते ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śiṣyavṛttikrameṇaiva vidyām āpnoti yaḥ śuciḥ |
brahmacaryavratasyāsya prathamaḥ pāda ucyate || 9 ||

lines.iast: śiṣyavṛttikrameṇaiva vidyām āpnoti yaḥ śuciḥ
lines.deva: शिष्यवृत्तिक्रमेणैव विद्यामाप्नोति यः शुचिः

lines.iast: brahmacaryavratasyāsya prathamaḥ pāda ucyate
lines.deva: ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतस्यास्य प्रथमः पाद उच्यते

padaccheda.iast: śiṣya-vṛtti-krameṇa eva vidyām āpnoti yaḥ śuciḥ brahmacarya-vratasya asya prathamaḥ pādaḥ ucyate
padaccheda.deva: शिष्य-वृत्ति-क्रमेण एव विद्याम् आप्नोति यः शुचिः ब्रह्मचर्य-व्रतस्य अस्य प्रथमः पादः उच्यते

words.meaning: by the course of a disciple's conduct

translations.text: That one who is pure gains knowledge only by the course of a disciple’s conduct (described from verse 5 on): this is called the first quarter of this vow of brahmacarya.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing verses 9–12: now he states brahmacarya with four quarters, in four verses.
Śaṅkara: śiṣyavṛttikrameṇa = by the course stated from ‘ācāryayonim iha’ on; that the pure man gains knowledge by it is the first quarter of this brahmacarya.

sanskrit.deva:
यथा नित्यं गुरौ वृत्तिर्गुरुपत्न्यां तथाचरेत् ।
तत्पुत्रे च तथा कुर्वन्द्वितीयः पाद उच्यते ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yathā nityaṃ gurau vṛttir gurupatnyāṃ tathācaret |
tatputre ca tathā kurvan dvitīyaḥ pāda ucyate || 10 ||

lines.iast: yathā nityaṃ gurau vṛttir gurupatnyāṃ tathācaret
lines.deva: यथा नित्यं गुरौ वृत्तिर्गुरुपत्न्यां तथाचरेत्

lines.iast: tatputre ca tathā kurvan dvitīyaḥ pāda ucyate
lines.deva: तत्पुत्रे च तथा कुर्वन्द्वितीयः पाद उच्यते

padaccheda.iast: yathā nityam gurau vṛttiḥ guru-patnyām tathā ācaret tat-putre ca tathā kurvan dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ucyate
padaccheda.deva: यथा नित्यम् गुरौ वृत्तिः गुरु-पत्न्याम् तथा आचरेत् तत्-पुत्रे च तथा कुर्वन् द्वितीयः पादः उच्यते

translations.text: As his conduct always is toward the teacher, so should he behave toward the teacher’s wife; doing so toward his son as well is called the second quarter.

notes: Śaṅkara: the verse is plain in meaning. He cites (Āpastamba) ‘conduct toward the teacher’s wives as toward the teacher’ and ‘conduct toward the teacher’s son as toward the teacher’.

sanskrit.deva:
आचार्येणात्मकृतं विजानञ्ज्ञात्वा चार्थं भावितोऽस्मीत्यनेन ।
यन्मन्यते तं प्रति हृष्टबुद्धिः स वै तृतीयो ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ācāryeṇātmakṛtaṃ vijānañ jñātvā cārthaṃ bhāvito 'smīty anena |
yan manyate taṃ prati hṛṣṭabuddhiḥ sa vai tṛtīyo brahmacaryasya pādaḥ || 11 ||

lines.iast: ācāryeṇātmakṛtaṃ vijānañ jñātvā cārthaṃ bhāvito 'smīty anena
lines.deva: आचार्येणात्मकृतं विजानञ्ज्ञात्वा चार्थं भावितोऽस्मीत्यनेन

lines.iast: yan manyate taṃ prati hṛṣṭabuddhiḥ sa vai tṛtīyo brahmacaryasya pādaḥ
lines.deva: यन्मन्यते तं प्रति हृष्टबुद्धिः स वै तृतीयो ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः

padaccheda.iast: ācāryeṇa ātma-kṛtam vijānan jñātvā ca artham bhāvitaḥ asmi iti anena yat manyate tam prati hṛṣṭa-buddhiḥ saḥ vai tṛtīyaḥ brahmacaryasya pādaḥ
padaccheda.deva: आचार्येण आत्म-कृतम् विजानन् ज्ञात्वा च अर्थम् भावितः अस्मि इति अनेन यत् मन्यते तम् प्रति हृष्ट-बुद्धिः सः वै तृतीयः ब्रह्मचर्यस्य पादः

words.meaning: what has been done for oneself

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Recognizing what the teacher has done for him, and having understood the meaning (of the Veda), he thinks, ‘I have been brought into being by him’, and, glad in mind toward him, (holds himself to have gained his end): that is the third quarter of brahmacarya.

notes: Śaṅkara: ātmakṛtam = the help done to oneself; artham = the meaning of the Veda, the highest human end; bhāvito ’smy anena = ‘I have been brought forth by him, rightly, as the Brahman that is my own nature, being, consciousness and bliss without a second’: so reflecting, glad in mind toward the teacher, he considers that he has gained his end (kṛtārthatva). That is the third quarter.

sanskrit.deva:
आचार्याय प्रियं कुर्यात्प्राणैरपि धनैरपि ।
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा चतुर्थः पाद उच्यते ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ācāryāya priyaṃ kuryāt prāṇair api dhanair api |
karmaṇā manasā vācā caturthaḥ pāda ucyate || 12 ||

lines.iast: ācāryāya priyaṃ kuryāt prāṇair api dhanair api
lines.deva: आचार्याय प्रियं कुर्यात्प्राणैरपि धनैरपि

lines.iast: karmaṇā manasā vācā caturthaḥ pāda ucyate
lines.deva: कर्मणा मनसा वाचा चतुर्थः पाद उच्यते

padaccheda.iast: ācāryāya priyam kuryāt prāṇaiḥ api dhanaiḥ api karmaṇā manasā vācā caturthaḥ pādaḥ ucyate
padaccheda.deva: आचार्याय प्रियम् कुर्यात् प्राणैः अपि धनैः अपि कर्मणा मनसा वाचा चतुर्थः पादः उच्यते

translations.text: He should do what is pleasing to the teacher, even with his life, even with his wealth, by deed, mind and speech: this is called the fourth quarter.

notes: Śaṅkara does not comment on this verse; it is the last of the four introduced before verse 9.

sanskrit.deva:
कालेन पादं लभते तथार्यं तथैव पादं गुरुयोगतश्च ।
उत्साहयोगेन च पादमृच्छेच्छास्त्रेण पादं च ततोऽभियाति ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kālena pādaṃ labhate tathāryaṃ tathaiva pādaṃ guruyogataś ca |
utsāhayogena ca pādam ṛcchec chāstreṇa pādaṃ ca tato 'bhiyāti || 13 ||

lines.iast: kālena pādaṃ labhate tathāryaṃ tathaiva pādaṃ guruyogataś ca
lines.deva: कालेन पादं लभते तथार्यं तथैव पादं गुरुयोगतश्च

lines.iast: utsāhayogena ca pādam ṛcchec chāstreṇa pādaṃ ca tato 'bhiyāti
lines.deva: उत्साहयोगेन च पादमृच्छेच्छास्त्रेण पादं च ततोऽभियाति

padaccheda.iast: kālena pādam labhate tathā āryam tathā eva pādam guru-yogataḥ ca utsāha-yogena ca pādam ṛcchet śāstreṇa pādam ca tataḥ abhiyāti
padaccheda.deva: कालेन पादम् लभते तथा आर्यम् तथा एव पादम् गुरु-योगतः च उत्साह-योगेन च पादम् ऋच्छेत् शास्त्रेण पादम् च ततः अभियाति

translations.text: By time he gains a noble quarter (of knowledge), and a quarter likewise from union with the teacher; by applied energy he reaches a quarter, and then by the teaching (enquired into with fellow students) he reaches a quarter.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: now he shows knowledge (vidyā) in four quarters.

Śaṅkara: no order is meant here. First (a quarter) from union with the teacher; then by applied energy, that is, by the rise of a special understanding; then by time, the ripening of understanding; then by the teaching, enquiry into the truth with fellow students. He cites a verse: ‘a quarter the disciple takes from the teacher, a quarter by his own intelligence, a quarter by time, a quarter with fellow students’.
Śaṅkara does not gloss tathāryam; it is read here as tathā āryam, ‘a noble (quarter)’.

sanskrit.deva:
ज्ञानादयो द्वादश यस्य रूपमन्यानि चाङ्गानि तथा बलं च ।
आचार्ययोगे फलतीति चाहुर्ब्रह्मार्थयोगेन च ब्रह्मचर्यम् ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
jñānādayo dvādaśa yasya rūpam anyāni cāṅgāni tathā balaṃ ca |
ācāryayoge phalatīti cāhur brahmārthayogena ca brahmacaryam || 14 ||

lines.iast: jñānādayo dvādaśa yasya rūpam anyāni cāṅgāni tathā balaṃ ca
lines.deva: ज्ञानादयो द्वादश यस्य रूपमन्यानि चाङ्गानि तथा बलं च

lines.iast: ācāryayoge phalatīti cāhur brahmārthayogena ca brahmacaryam
lines.deva: आचार्ययोगे फलतीति चाहुर्ब्रह्मार्थयोगेन च ब्रह्मचर्यम्

padaccheda.iast: jñāna-ādayaḥ dvādaśa yasya rūpam anyāni ca aṅgāni tathā balam ca ācārya-yoge phalati iti ca āhuḥ brahma-artha-yogena ca brahmacaryam
padaccheda.deva: ज्ञान-आदयः द्वादश यस्य रूपम् अन्यानि च अङ्गानि तथा बलम् च आचार्य-योगे फलति इति च आहुः ब्रह्म-अर्थ-योगेन च ब्रह्मचर्यम्

words.meaning: by joining to the purpose of Brahman

translations.text: (The man) whose form is knowledge and the other twelve (virtues), the other limbs too, and the strength (to keep them): (all this) bears fruit (only) in union with the teacher, they say; and brahmacarya (bears fruit) by its joining to the purpose of Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: knowledge and the rest bear fruit in the presence of the teacher.

Śaṅkara: jñānādayaḥ = the twelve virtues stated before, beginning ‘jñānaṃ ca’ (2.19), of the man whose form they are; the other limbs = those stated in the two verses ‘śreyāṃs tu ṣaḍvidhas tyāgaḥ’ (2.25) and ‘satyaṃ dhyānam’ (2.28); balam = the power to maintain those dharmas. All this bears fruit only in union with the teacher, not without it. He cites Chāndogya 4.9.3 (‘knowledge learned from a teacher’) and 6.14.2 (‘a man who has a teacher knows’). brahmacaryam: the service and the rest done in the teacher’s presence bears fruit by joining to the purpose of Brahman, that is, by bringing about the oneness of one’s own Self with Brahman, being, consciousness and bliss without a second.

sanskrit.deva:
एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण देवा देवत्वमाप्नुवन् ।
ऋषयश्च महाभागा ब्रह्मचर्येण चाभवन् ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
etena brahmacaryeṇa devā devatvam āpnuvan |
ṛṣayaś ca mahābhāgā brahmacaryeṇa cābhavan || 15 ||

lines.iast: etena brahmacaryeṇa devā devatvam āpnuvan
lines.deva: एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण देवा देवत्वमाप्नुवन्

lines.iast: ṛṣayaś ca mahābhāgā brahmacaryeṇa cābhavan
lines.deva: ऋषयश्च महाभागा ब्रह्मचर्येण चाभवन्

padaccheda.iast: etena brahmacaryeṇa devāḥ devatvam āpnuvan ṛṣayaḥ ca mahā-bhāgāḥ brahmacaryeṇa ca abhavan
padaccheda.deva: एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण देवाः देवत्वम् आप्नुवन् ऋषयः च महा-भागाः ब्रह्मचर्येण च अभवन्

translations.text: By this brahmacarya the gods gained godhood, and by brahmacarya the greatly blessed seers became (seers).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing verses 15–16: he praises brahmacarya in two verses.
Śaṅkara: the gods gained godhood by it; the seers too gained seerhood by it.

sanskrit.deva:
एतेनैव सगन्धर्वा रूपमप्सरसोऽजयन् ।
एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण सूर्य अह्नाय जायते ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
etenaiva sagandharvā rūpam apsaraso 'jayan |
etena brahmacaryeṇa sūrya ahnāya jāyate || 16 ||

lines.iast: etenaiva sagandharvā rūpam apsaraso 'jayan
lines.deva: एतेनैव सगन्धर्वा रूपमप्सरसोऽजयन्

lines.iast: etena brahmacaryeṇa sūrya ahnāya jāyate
lines.deva: एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण सूर्य अह्नाय जायते

padaccheda.iast: etena eva sa-gandharvāḥ rūpam apsarasaḥ ajayan etena brahmacaryeṇa sūryaḥ ahnāya jāyate
padaccheda.deva: एतेन एव स-गन्धर्वाः रूपम् अप्सरसः अजयन् एतेन ब्रह्मचर्येण सूर्यः अह्नाय जायते

translations.text: By this very (brahmacarya) the Apsarases, with the Gandharvas, won beauty; by this brahmacarya the sun comes into being, to light (the worlds).

notes: Śaṅkara: sagandharvāḥ = together with the Gandharvas; rūpam = lovely forms, which they won by this brahmacarya. ahna = a mass of radiance; ahnāya = to illuminate the worlds, the sun comes into being. He cites ‘ahna is also called radiance’.

sanskrit.deva:
आकाङ्क्षार्थस्य संयोगाद्रसभेदार्थिनामिव ।
एवं ह्येतत्समाज्ञाय तादृग्भावं गता इमे ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ākāṅkṣārthasya saṃyogād rasabhedārthinām iva |
evaṃ hy etat samājñāya tādṛgbhāvaṃ gatā ime || 17 ||

lines.iast: ākāṅkṣārthasya saṃyogād rasabhedārthinām iva
lines.deva: आकाङ्क्षार्थस्य संयोगाद्रसभेदार्थिनामिव

lines.iast: evaṃ hy etat samājñāya tādṛgbhāvaṃ gatā ime
lines.deva: एवं ह्येतत्समाज्ञाय तादृग्भावं गता इमे

padaccheda.iast: ākāṅkṣā-arthasya saṃyogāt rasa-bheda-arthinām iva evam hi etat samājñāya tādṛk-bhāvam gatāḥ ime
padaccheda.deva: आकाङ्क्षा-अर्थस्य संयोगात् रस-भेद-अर्थिनाम् इव एवम् हि एतत् समाज्ञाय तादृक्-भावम् गताः इमे

words.meaning: of those who seek different flavours

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: As (wish-fulfilling gems give) to those who seek different flavours (each what he seeks), through union with the thing desired, (so brahmacarya gives each his desire); understanding this thus, these (gods and the rest) have reached such a state.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: how does the one brahmacarya bring about fruits of many kinds?

Śaṅkara: as the wish-fulfilling gem and the like give to those who seek different flavours the very thing each desires, through union with the thing desired, so this brahmacarya gives whatever is desired. Knowing this, and practising brahmacarya for this fruit or that, these, the gods and the rest, reached such a state. Since the highest human end comes from brahmacarya practised in the teacher’s presence, one should enter the womb that is the teacher, become an embryo, and practise brahmacarya.

sanskrit.deva:
अन्तवन्तः क्षत्रिय ते जयन्ति लोकाञ्जनाः कर्मणा निर्मितेन ।
ज्ञानेन विद्वांस्तेज अभ्येति नित्यं न विद्यते ह्यन्यथा तस्य पन्थाः ॥ १८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
antavantaḥ kṣatriya te jayanti lokāñ janāḥ karmaṇā nirmitena |
jñānena vidvāṃs teja abhyeti nityaṃ na vidyate hy anyathā tasya panthāḥ || 18 ||

lines.iast: antavantaḥ kṣatriya te jayanti lokāñ janāḥ karmaṇā nirmitena
lines.deva: अन्तवन्तः क्षत्रिय ते जयन्ति लोकाञ्जनाः कर्मणा निर्मितेन

lines.iast: jñānena vidvāṃs teja abhyeti nityaṃ na vidyate hy anyathā tasya panthāḥ
lines.deva: ज्ञानेन विद्वांस्तेज अभ्येति नित्यं न विद्यते ह्यन्यथा तस्य पन्थाः

padaccheda.iast: antavantaḥ kṣatriya te jayanti lokān janāḥ karmaṇā nirmitena jñānena vidvān tejaḥ abhyeti nityam na vidyate hi anyathā tasya panthāḥ
padaccheda.deva: अन्तवन्तः क्षत्रिय ते जयन्ति लोकान् जनाः कर्मणा निर्मितेन ज्ञानेन विद्वान् तेजः अभ्येति नित्यम् न विद्यते हि अन्यथा तस्य पन्थाः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. ins. sg.

translations.text: Worlds that have an end, O warrior, those men win by action they have wrought. By knowledge the knower reaches the eternal light; for there is no other path to it.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: to the doubt that the human end comes not from steadfastness in knowledge but from action alone, he says this.

Śaṅkara: antavantaḥ, read with lokān = worlds that have an end, the worlds of the ancestors, of the gods and the rest; men do not win by action the endless world, the supreme Self that is their own Self. By knowledge, not by action, the knower reaches the eternal light, imperishable, his own Self. Why by knowledge alone? Because for that light of full bliss there is no path but knowledge. He cites Śvetāśvatara 3.8 (‘knowing him thus one goes beyond death; there is no other path for going’).

sanskrit.deva:
आभाति शुक्लमिव लोहितमिवाथो कृष्णमथार्जुनं काद्रवं वा ।
यद्ब्राह्मणः पश्यति यत्र विद्वान्कथंरूपं तदमृतमक्षरं परम् ॥ १९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ābhāti śuklam iva lohitam ivātho kṛṣṇam athārjunaṃ kādravaṃ vā |
yad brāhmaṇaḥ paśyati yatra vidvān kathaṃrūpaṃ tad amṛtam akṣaraṃ param || 19 ||

lines.iast: ābhāti śuklam iva lohitam ivātho kṛṣṇam athārjunaṃ kādravaṃ vā
lines.deva: आभाति शुक्लमिव लोहितमिवाथो कृष्णमथार्जुनं काद्रवं वा

lines.iast: yad brāhmaṇaḥ paśyati yatra vidvān kathaṃrūpaṃ tad amṛtam akṣaraṃ param
lines.deva: यद्ब्राह्मणः पश्यति यत्र विद्वान्कथंरूपं तदमृतमक्षरं परम्

padaccheda.iast: ābhāti śuklam iva lohitam iva atho kṛṣṇam atha arjunam kādravam vā yat brāhmaṇaḥ paśyati yatra vidvān kathaṃ-rūpam tat amṛtam akṣaram param
padaccheda.deva: आभाति शुक्लम् इव लोहितम् इव अथो कृष्णम् अथ अर्जुनम् काद्रवम् वा यत् ब्राह्मणः पश्यति यत्र विद्वान् कथं-रूपम् तत् अमृतम् अक्षरम् परम्

translations.text: Does it appear as if white, or as if red, or black, or silver-white, or tawny, that which the brāhmaṇa, the knower, sees, (and) where? Of what form is that deathless, imperishable, supreme (Brahman)?

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: what does the Brahman that the knower sees by knowledge appear like? Dhṛtarāṣṭra asks.

Śaṅkara: does the Brahman the knower sees by knowledge appear as if white, as if red, as if black, silver-white or tawny? In what place does it shine? Of what form is that deathless, imperishable, supreme Brahman?

sanskrit.deva:
नाभाति शुक्लमिव लोहितमिवाथो कृष्णमथार्जुनं वा काद्रवं वा ।
न पृथिव्यां तिष्ठति नान्तरिक्षे नैतत्समुद्रे सलिलं बिभर्ति ॥ २० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
nābhāti śuklam iva lohitam ivātho kṛṣṇam athārjunaṃ vā kādravaṃ vā |
na pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhati nāntarikṣe naitat samudre salilaṃ bibharti || 20 ||

lines.iast: nābhāti śuklam iva lohitam ivātho kṛṣṇam athārjunaṃ vā kādravaṃ vā
lines.deva: नाभाति शुक्लमिव लोहितमिवाथो कृष्णमथार्जुनं वा काद्रवं वा

lines.iast: na pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhati nāntarikṣe naitat samudre salilaṃ bibharti
lines.deva: न पृथिव्यां तिष्ठति नान्तरिक्षे नैतत्समुद्रे सलिलं बिभर्ति

padaccheda.iast: na ābhāti śuklam iva lohitam iva atho kṛṣṇam atha arjunam vā kādravam vā na pṛthivyām tiṣṭhati na antarikṣe na etat samudre salilam bibharti
padaccheda.deva: न आभाति शुक्लम् इव लोहितम् इव अथो कृष्णम् अथ अर्जुनम् वा काद्रवम् वा न पृथिव्याम् तिष्ठति न अन्तरिक्षे न एतत् समुद्रे सलिलम् बिभर्ति

translations.text: It does not appear as if white, or as if red, or black, or silver-white, or tawny. It does not stand on the earth, nor in the mid-region; it does not bear water in the ocean (a body made of the elements).

notes: Śaṅkara: Brahman does not appear in the form of white and the rest, because it is formless. He cites Śvetāśvatara 3.10 (‘what is higher than that is formless and free from ill’) and Kaṭha 1.3.15 (‘without sound, without touch, without form’). Nor does it stand on the earth or in the mid-region: scripture shows that it rests in nothing else, Chāndogya 7.24.1 (‘on what does it rest, sir?’ ‘On its own greatness’).

Śaṅkara: why does it not stand on the earth and the rest? Because it does not bear water in the ocean, that is, it bears no body made of the five elements. The word salila stands for the five elements, as ap does in ‘he first created the waters and placed his seed in them’ (Manu 1.8); and in Chāndogya 5.9.1 (‘in the fifth offering the waters come to be called man’) the waters themselves are called man. The sense: were Brahman within saṃsāra, it would, having entered saṃsāra, have colour and form like a pot and rest in something else; but this Brahman, having nothing before it and the rest, has not entered saṃsāra. Therefore it is without colour and form.

sanskrit.deva:
नैवर्क्षु तन्न यजुःषु नाप्यथर्वसु न दृश्यते वै विमलेषु सामसु ।
रथन्तरे बार्हते वापि राजन्महाव्रतस्यात्मनि दृश्यते तत् ॥ २१ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
naivarkṣu tan na yajuḥṣu nāpy atharvasu na dṛśyate vai vimaleṣu sāmasu |
rathantare bārhate vāpi rājan mahāvratasyātmani dṛśyate tat || 21 ||

lines.iast: naivarkṣu tan na yajuḥṣu nāpy atharvasu na dṛśyate vai vimaleṣu sāmasu
lines.deva: नैवर्क्षु तन्न यजुःषु नाप्यथर्वसु न दृश्यते वै विमलेषु सामसु

lines.iast: rathantare bārhate vāpi rājan mahāvratasyātmani dṛśyate tat
lines.deva: रथन्तरे बार्हते वापि राजन्महाव्रतस्यात्मनि दृश्यते तत्

padaccheda.iast: na eva ṛkṣu tat na yajuḥṣu na api atharvasu na dṛśyate vai vimaleṣu sāmasu rathantare bārhate vā api rājan mahāvratasya ātmani dṛśyate tat
padaccheda.deva: न एव ऋक्षु तत् न यजुःषु न अपि अथर्वसु न दृश्यते वै विमलेषु सामसु रथन्तरे बार्हते वा अपि राजन् महाव्रतस्य आत्मनि दृश्यते तत्

translations.text: It is not seen in the Ṛc verses, nor in the Yajus formulas, nor in the Atharvan hymns, nor in the stainless Sāman chants, nor even in the Rathantara or the Bṛhat chant, O king: it is seen in the self of one of great vows.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the verse: then is it not perceived by anyone anywhere? He says this.

Śaṅkara: mahāvratasya = of one endowed with the virtues stated from ‘jñānaṃ ca satyaṃ ca’ to ‘mahāvratā dvādaśa brāhmaṇasya’ (2.19): in his self the supreme Brahman is seen. It is not established as ‘this’, like a pot, but in the self, as the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
अवारणीयं तमसः परस्तात्तदन्ततोऽभ्येति विनाशकाले ।
अणीयरूपं च तथाप्यणीयसां महत्स्वरूपं त्वपि पर्वतेभ्यः ॥ २२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
avāraṇīyaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt tad antato 'bhyeti vināśakāle |
aṇīyarūpaṃ ca tathāpy aṇīyasāṃ mahatsvarūpaṃ tv api parvatebhyaḥ || 22 ||

lines.iast: avāraṇīyaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt tad antato 'bhyeti vināśakāle
lines.deva: अवारणीयं तमसः परस्तात्तदन्ततोऽभ्येति विनाशकाले

lines.iast: aṇīyarūpaṃ ca tathāpy aṇīyasāṃ mahatsvarūpaṃ tv api parvatebhyaḥ
lines.deva: अणीयरूपं च तथाप्यणीयसां महत्स्वरूपं त्वपि पर्वतेभ्यः

padaccheda.iast: avāraṇīyam tamasaḥ parastāt tat antataḥ abhyeti vināśa-kāle aṇīya-rūpam ca tathā api aṇīyasām mahat-svarūpam tu api parvatebhyaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अवारणीयम् तमसः परस्तात् तत् अन्ततः अभ्येति विनाश-काले अणीय-रूपम् च तथा अपि अणीयसाम् महत्-स्वरूपम् तु अपि पर्वतेभ्यः

translations.text: (What is seen in the self of one of great vows is Brahman,) not to be obstructed, beyond darkness (ignorance); to it (the world) goes at the end, at the time of destruction. It is smaller in form than the smallest, and greater in its nature than the mountains.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing verses 22–23: now he states its nature, the seeing of it and its fruit, in two verses.

Śaṅkara: what is seen in the self of one of great vows is Brahman, not to be obstructed because it goes everywhere; tamasaḥ = ignorance, beyond which it is. tad antato ’bhyeti vināśakāle: to that Brahman the world goes at the end, at the time of destruction, the dissolution (pralaya). He cites Kaṭha 1.2.20 (‘smaller than the small, greater than the great’).

sanskrit.deva:
तदेतदह्ना संस्थितं भाति सर्वं तदात्मवित्पश्यति ज्ञानयोगात् ।
तस्मिञ्जगत्सर्वमिदं प्रतिष्ठितं य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥ २३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad etad ahnā saṃsthitaṃ bhāti sarvaṃ tad ātmavit paśyati jñānayogāt |
tasmiñ jagat sarvam idaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti || 23 ||

lines.iast: tad etad ahnā saṃsthitaṃ bhāti sarvaṃ tad ātmavit paśyati jñānayogāt
lines.deva: तदेतदह्ना संस्थितं भाति सर्वं तदात्मवित्पश्यति ज्ञानयोगात्

lines.iast: tasmiñ jagat sarvam idaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
lines.deva: तस्मिञ्जगत्सर्वमिदं प्रतिष्ठितं य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति

padaccheda.iast: tat etat ahnā saṃsthitam bhāti sarvam tat ātma-vit paśyati jñāna-yogāt tasmin jagat sarvam idam pratiṣṭhitam ye etat viduḥ amṛtāḥ te bhavanti
padaccheda.deva: तत् एतत् अह्ना संस्थितम् भाति सर्वम् तत् आत्म-वित् पश्यति ज्ञान-योगात् तस्मिन् जगत् सर्वम् इदम् प्रतिष्ठितम् ये एतत् विदुः अमृताः ते भवन्ति

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: All this (world), set (in Brahman) by its light, shines (as Brahman). That the knower of the Self sees by the yoga of knowledge. In it this whole world is established. Those who know this become deathless.

notes: Śaṅkara: the smallness, greatness and the rest that are seen in the world: all this world, set in Brahman by its light (ahnā = in the form of the day, of light), shines as that very Brahman. He cites Kaṭha 2.2.15 (‘by its light all this shines’) and ‘kindled by whose radiance the sun gives heat’. That Brahman the knower of the Self sees by the yoga of knowledge, not by the yoga of action. In that supreme Self this whole world is established; those who know this become deathless.
